subject: Materials Science
title: Gorilla Glass: Phones That Survive Falls
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Gorilla Glass: Phones That Survive Falls.

hook.text: Your phone screen survives drops that would shatter a wine glass. Chemistry is the reason.

buildup.text: Gorilla Glass starts as standard aluminosilicate glass — thin and clear but fragile.

discovery.text: Ion exchange soaks it in molten potassium salt — big K⁺ ions replace small Na⁺ ions.

twist.text: The larger ions squeeze into the surface, creating extreme compressive stress that resists cracks.

climax.text: Over 8 billion devices worldwide use chemically strengthened glass on their screens.

punchline.text: Swapping tiny atoms for big ones armor-plates your phone screen.

quiz.question: How is Gorilla Glass strengthened?
options: By adding a plastic film on top
By ion exchange that creates surface compression
